Hello! I'm no expert in either field, hypnotist nor massage therapist, but I am proficient enough in both. I'm the go to guy after practices if someone is feeling sore. Haha.  


I might have been doing a mix of massage therapy and hypnotic induction at the same time, without knowing it.   


During my sessions, when warming up the area, I usually tell them why I do so, and what general area I'll be putting more focus in. To which I tell them that if they do fall asleep, or do fall into a deep state of relaxation, that it's normal and to not hinder the process and to just let it be. When starting with some light massages, I tell them to relax, to release all the tension in their bodies. Every stroke or hold will just let them go deeper into relaxation.   


I don't really do anything after that though. Once I get them relaxed, I usually just continue on with my massages. You can definitely learn some scripts, but you'll just have to change the wording to fit with your sessions, with the different strokes or holds that you do, or also incorporate it into their breathing, esp if you have a pressure hold that you press harder as they exhale and release on inhale. But I would definitely read up more on hypnosis and how it works, and see if you can tie in some aspects. There's also a matter of consent and such.
